 Print CLAT 2027 admit card expected between November 21 and 26; check exam schedule and download details CLAT 2027 admit card : The Consortium of National Law Universities (NLUs) is expected to release the Common Law Admission Test (CLAT) 2027 admit card soon. As of November 21, candidates awaiting the undergraduate (UG) and postgraduate (PG) entrance examination hall tickets should monitor the official website, consortiumofnlus.ac.in, for the download link. The admit card is expected between November 21 and November 26, 2026. However, the Consortium has not officially confirmed the exact release date. Registered candidates will have to log in using their registered mobile number and password to access the hall ticket. The examination is scheduled for December 6, 2026. CLAT 2027 examination and admission schedule The CLAT 2027 examination will take place in offline mode from 2 PM to 4 PM. Candidates appearing for the examination should keep track of the subsequent answer key, result and counselling announcements. The following timeline outlines the expected admission process: Event 
 Date 
 Admit card
 November 21-26, 2026 (expected)
 CLAT 2027 examination
 December 6, 2026
 Provisional answer key
 December 7-10, 2026 (tentative)
 Objection window
 December 9-11, 2026 (tentative)
 Final answer key and results
 Third week of December 2026
 Counselling registration
 Last week of December 2026
 First allotment list
 First week of January 2027
 Seats available and competition CLAT 2027 admission covers 26 participating NLUs, offering approximately 5,542 seats. These include 3,952 UG seats across five-year integrated law programmes and 1,590 PG seats across one-year LL.M. programmes. NLSIU Bengaluru has 370 seats across programmes, including 310 B.A. LL.B. seats. Other large intakes include MNLU Nagpur (300), NLU Jodhpur (284), WBNUJS Kolkata (282) and NUSRL Ranchi (270). The previous examination cycle recorded 92,344 registrations, comprising 75,009 UG and 17,335 PG applicants. Of these, 88,657 candidates appeared, representing 96.01% attendance. Earlier registration figures were 78,914 in 2025, 67,590 in 2024 and 54,253 in 2023. Join conversation

 • Direct link to visit the official CLAT 2027 website CLAT 2027 UG exam pattern The UG paper will contain 120 passage-based multiple-choice questions, to be completed in 120 minutes. Eligible PwD candidates will receive 160 minutes. Each correct answer carries one mark, while an incorrect response attracts a deduction of 0.25 marks. Unattempted questions carry no penalty. The five sections are Current Affairs and General Knowledge (25%), Legal Reasoning (25%), English Language (20%), Logical Reasoning (20%) and Quantitative Techniques (10%). Candidates should check the official portal regularly for the admit card and subsequent announcements.
